analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) host leaders Almería in the last game of round 15. One report says Sergio Lobera returned to Ceuta as coach on 8 November, so this would be his second league game; Almería host Andorra first, and Marcos Luna, who limped off at Girona, should have served his yellow-card ban by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, with 1.4 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta have scored once in their last three league games and Almería's recent league games have been tight (1-0, 1-1, 2-2). Almería should be favourites, but a high-scoring game needs Ceuta to contribute more than they have been.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with 6.0 for Ceuta. I lean lower: the bottom side winning six corners at home to the leaders looks generous, even if Lobera wants Ceuta to keep the ball more. Almería's share should be higher and Ceuta's lower, with a slightly smaller total.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. A desperate home side against the leaders points up, but a new coach usually starts by demanding discipline, so I hold at the site's number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, with 18.9 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta have not shown that kind of volume (they failed to score at Córdoba or at home to Sporting), and Almería's games are more controlled, with 12 shots each at Girona.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Ceuta's attack has been blunt and Almería's recent wins have been narrow. Miguel de la Fuente, the league's top scorer, is the likeliest source of efforts on target.
